name: Hanuman Temple, Simdega
town_description: Simdega is a small district headquarters town in south-western Jharkhand, carved out of Gumla district on 30 April 2001. It sits amid the forested hills of the Chota Nagpur Plateau with a predominantly tribal population and is known for its hockey tradition (home to Olympic medalists). Tourist draws include Ramrekha Dham (~26 km), the Kelaghagh dam on the Chhinda river (~4 km, boating/parasailing), Ketunga Dham, and Bhairo Baba Pahari.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi - about 137-160 km from Simdega town (verify exact distance)
travel.railway: No direct rail link at Simdega town; nearby stations include Bano and Pokla
travel.road: NH 143 and state roads; well connected by bus and private vehicles to Ranchi, Gumla and Rourkela (Odisha)

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant winter); Tuesdays and Hanuman Jayanti are busier
